q: The Jewett-Krieger theorem constructs a uniquely ergodic minimal topological model for any ergodic MPT. The relevance to the isomorphism problem is that:
opts: Topological models are not unique: different Jewett-Krieger models of the same abstract ergodic system can be topologically inequivalent — measure-theoretic isomorphism is coarser than topological conjugacy
Unique ergodicity implies the system is Bernoulli
All models have the same topological entropy
exp: The Jewett-Krieger theorem shows every abstract ergodic system has a uniquely ergodic minimal topological model, but this model is far from unique (many topologically inequivalent models exist). Topological conjugacy is strictly finer than measure-theoretic isomorphism: the latter is the 'right' notion for ergodic theory.
